correctness.rationale: For Q>4 and 1<m<Q/4, direct integration of the published stationary gas and droplet profiles proves a strict one-crossing likelihood threshold at b=log(m)/Q. Positive signed mass gives TV=(Phi(z)-1)/m. Implicit differentiation yields Dprime=(1-z(a+1-z)/Q)/m². The exact 0<dz/da<z/a inequality makes its numerator strictly decreasing, classifying monotonicity versus a unique interior maximum. Taylor inversion of F at the upper gas fold proves the nonzero negative 3/2 correction and divergent curvature. Every stated parameter and one-sided boundary is accounted for; standalone verify.py passed 2180 bounded checks, which are diagnostics, not universal proof.

value.rationale: The stationary coexistence profiles naturally define two competing one-particle spatial experiments. The exact optimal discriminator and its error quantify physical phase observability. The mathematical shape changes qualitatively with crowding Q: Q=5 has strictly increasing TV, while Q=20 has a unique interior peak even as condensed mass grows. The upper-fold nonanalytic 3/2 correction gives an exact and nontrivial critical asymptotic. These resolve motivated observability features but do not assert a new phase or microscopic theorem.
